column1: # hazards.tsv — the migration hazard table, read by com.vaadin.swingbridge.migration.tool.HazardScan.
# One row per detection rule. Tab-separated:
#     id
column3: label [

column1: # `id` the H_ slug this row shares with its bullet's anchor in
#           migration/1-swing-to-emulators/spec.md. HazardTableTest joins the two by slug in both
#           directions, so a row naming a hazard the spec dropped — or a spec bullet with a
#           `Detect:` grep that no row implements — reddens the build. Several rows may carry one
#           id when a hazard has more than one signal (the timezone buckets; the HTML-pane pair).
# `section` where that bullet lives: §7 (known migration hazards) or §5 (import-rewrite sharp edges
#           no optimize-imports pass catches).
# `regex`   java.util.regex, matched per line as `grep -n` does. Omit the column for a manual row;
#           its label then renders as a checklist item instead of a scanned section.
# `glob`    which files to read it over. Omitted means *.java.
# THIS FILE IS THE PATTERNS' ONLY HOME. It replaced hazard-scan.sh, whose ~100 lines of bash held a
# second hand-synced copy of spec.md §7's `Detect:` lines — and had already drifted from them.
# RETIRED PATTERNS, so the next maintainer does not "add one back":
#   - Toolkit, GraphicsEnvironment: both gained swap-table rows (D_graphics_environment), so the
#     hazard cannot occur — the reference rewrites. What retires a "headless JDK class survives the
#     swap" hazard is the row, not the import-swap tool deleting the java.awt.* import: deletion
#     re-emits stay-JDK types verbatim. A scan for a hazard that cannot occur trains the migrator
#     to ignore the scan.
#   - A bare getInstance() pattern for the static-frame hazard: it matches Calendar.getInstance()
#     and every other factory. A subclass-typed holder (`static MainFrame INSTANCE`) is caught by
#     the ArchUnit gate, which resolves the type hierarchy; no name-based pattern can.
#   - HTMLDocument *reads*: getElement / getDefaultRootElement resolve (D_htmldocument). Only the
#     mutators are dead, so a bare HTMLDocument/getElement pattern is now all false positives.
H_system_exit
column3: System.exit / Runtime exit-halt  [ArchUnit-gated]
